_comment: Wording for the Customize screen's raw-YAML disclaimer, kept out of the component so the text can be edited without reading JSX. Rendered by ./CustomizeYamlNotice.tsx. Delete this file and that component when Customize gets a real visual editor.
title: Raw YAML, for now
summary: Until there is a proper editor, your dashboard is a config file.
paragraphs: Adding things is the easy part: apps you install through MOS appear on your dashboard by themselves, and Add to Homepage covers the rest — an app already running on your network, or an ordinary website link.

Layout is another story. Grouping, ordering, renaming, moving things around: all of that still means editing this file by hand. Until we build something better, the quickest way through is to let an AI assistant do the fiddly part.
steps: Copy everything in the editor and paste it into a text file or a note. That is your undo.
Paste it into any AI assistant and describe the layout you want in plain language — "move Photos above Files", "rename this group to Media", "put the media apps in one column".
Paste its version back over everything in the editor and press Save and apply. Malformed YAML is refused, so a bad answer costs you a red message, not your dashboard.
Open your dashboard and look. If something is missing, paste your copy back and save again.
callout: Don't ask an assistant to add an app for you. It will happily invent one you don't run, at an address that doesn't exist, and still hand you perfectly valid YAML.
